problems.reason: Sentence 7 repeats the same claim about the individual being a subadult male twice.
Sentence 6 repeats the same explanation of the death scenario twice.
Sentence 3 refers to a species named Aurorazhdarcho micronyx, which is not the main subject of the page (Aurorazhdarcho).
Both sentences describe the holotype skeleton as a nearly complete specimen preserved on a single slab.
The sentence refers to "missing skull and neck elements" without having previously introduced that these elements are missing.
It mentions "fused ischiopubes" and the absence of a wide birth canal without prior context explaining these anatomical features.
It states the genus holds the distinction of being the oldest known azhdarchoid, which is a classification claim rather than a direct attribute of the animal itself.

The page alternately names the type species as Aurorazhdarcho primordius (sentences 9, 13) and as Aurorazhdarcho micronyx (sentence 7), and gives conflicting dates for the holotype (1757‑1779 vs 2011).
Sentence 11 repeats the same claim about the holotype being a subadult male, citing fused ischiopubes and lack of a wide egg‑laying canal twice.
